thread:
anya: Quick heads-up — embeddings mismatch between HF conversion and Redwood reranker tests.

kai: what's the symptom?

anya: On the same HF model, Redwood's embed endpoint returns vectors that differ depending on tokenizer/pooling choices. Reranker NDCG@10 drops ~6-8% when using `cls` pooling vs `mean` on our eval.

sanjay: did we accidentally drop CLS during conversion? I remember some tokenizers set `add_prefix_space` and change offsets.

anya: I diffed tokenized outputs — HF tokenizer (hub) yields tokens like [CLS] ... [SEP] while our converted tokenizer sometimes strips BOS/EOS. Example snippet from converted `tokenizer_config.json`:

```json
{"special_tokens_map": {"cls_token": "[CLS]","sep_token": "[SEP]","pad_token": "[PAD]"}, "tokenizer_config": {"add_prefix_space": false}}
```

dana: also saw truncation strategy mismatch — HF default was `longest_first` for pairs, but our conversion used `only_first` for single sequences. That can drop the leading special token if truncation is applied incorrectly.

ml-ci-bot: test run 2026-02-18T12:04Z — embed-regression-check failed: ndcg_delta: -0.073 (threshold -0.02)

kai: can you paste the conversion args you used?

anya: conversion was: `tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, local_files_only=True)` then `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'cls_token':'[CLS]'})` then `tokenizer.save_pretrained(out)`. Redwood's conversion pipeline used a wrapper flag `--strip_bos_eos true` by default — suspect default stripping.

sanjay: proposed quick test: run tokenizer-diff on 1k examples and count occurrences of CLS/SEP ids in `input_ids`. If missing, pooling config `pooling: cls` will index the wrong token.

dana: ack. Also note quantization experiments introduced a separate small drift: with int8 quant + KV-cache optimizations, the first token embedding cosine similarity shifted ~0.4 on some inputs. Might be compounding the reranker drop.

anya: reproduction steps I ran: 

```bash
# minimal repro
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local/model'); print(t.encode('Hello world', add_special_tokens=True))"
# compare with redwood conversion
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('converted-tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('Hello world'))"
# then call redwood embed endpoint and dump input_ids, pooling index
curl -s -X POST https://redwood/api/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{\"input\": \"Hello world\"}' | jq .
```

kai: action items: (1) run tokenizer-diff on 1k seeded examples and produce a CSV of missing special tokens, (2) confirm conversion flags (`strip_bos_eos`, `add_prefix_space`, `use_fast`), (3) run embed/regression with `pooling: mean` vs `pooling: cls` to isolate pooling impact, (4) re-run int8 quant tests with KV-cache disabled.

anya: assigning to @sanjay and @dana, I'll attach the failing eval set and diffs to the ticket.

sanjay: I'll push a small script `eng-ml/tests/tokenizer_diff.py` tomorrow and share results. ping me if you want access earlier.

dana: noted, will also try disabling the int8-KV patch and re-run the eval.

kai: thx :thumbsup: 

anya: one more note — for chat templates, we must ensure system prompts are not being prepended/stripped differently between HF chat-conversion and Redwood chat-wrapper; that changes token offsets for CLS/SEP. I'll add a quick checklist for chat template parity.

ml-ci-bot: created issue ML-6212: "tokenizer/packing/pooling mismatch causing embed regressions" (assigned: sanjay, dana)
